redFirst.basis: Regression task, expectRedFirst false, and the fix is in the CASES: audit-status.py's executable bytes are unchanged (only _shell_word's docstring grew), so HEAD's code under the new cases is green by design and the helper has no red to find. The reproduction was watched on HEAD before any edit: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --spaced tests/test_audit_status.py` -> FAIL kt5, kt7, kt9, kt9b, kt6b, kt8, 'SELFTEST FAILED: 401/407 cases passed', 0/1 files ok. That the corrected cases can fail was proven in a throwaway git-archive export (not the shared tree): _shell_word mutated to `return text` (unquoted) -> under --spaced, kt5, kt7, kt9, kt9b, kt6b, kt8 FAIL, 401/407, exit 1. outcome.technical: Diagnosis. The CI rows quote a kept tree's path with shlex.quote (POSIX sh) because the path holds a space (linux stress, spaced TMPDIR) or backslashes (Windows). The cases looked for the bare path, so kt5/kt7/kt9/kt9b compared a spelling a shell would split in two. kt6b's guard `named in rows[0]` failed on the quoting, so it ran nothing (ran=None). kt8's save filter `-C <bare tree> ` matched nothing (saves=[]). The brief reads kt6b as a real/ vs via/ mismatch, which does not match the log: the case realpaths its base, and the linux log's row and fixture both carry real/ (122912183449.log:572), so the miss was the quoting. The product is right for the shell it targets. Every command this plugin prints or runs is quoted with shlex.quote for a POSIX shell, and _proc_group.locate_sh resolves that shell on Windows too (Git for Windows' sh; it never falls back to cmd.exe). The plugin has no cmd.exe or PowerShell quoting helper to match, and I wrote no second copy of a helper. Product change: _shell_word's docstring (plugins/audit/scripts/status/audit-status.py:2080) now says which shell the rows target (sh/bash, Git for Windows' sh on Windows, not cmd.exe or PowerShell) and that git's own sh reads the inner submodule-foreach command. No executable byte changed. Case changes (tests/test_audit_status.py): new helpers _posix_words (shlex.split, None on an unbalanced quote), _remedy_after (the command after a row's ` <path> - `), _run_as_written (runs the printed text under _proc_group.shell_invocation, the plugin's own resolved POSIX shell, so Windows uses git's sh and not a bare `sh` on PATH; None reads as failure) and _listed_worktrees/_one_spelling (realpath plus normcase, because git lists forward slashes on Windows). kt5, kt9 and kt9b now assert the words a POSIX shell reads equal ['git','worktree','remove',('--force',) <path>]. kt7 asserts exactly 2 save lines, the update-ref pin once, and one foreach push whose inner command reads the tree as one word. kt6b now runs the row's printed text as written instead of rebuilding argv by split(' '). It also checks that git listed the tree BEFORE the remove, in the spelling the after-check reads, so 'lists it no more' is a watched change and cannot pass because the spellings never matched. kt8 picks its saves by the -C word a shell reads and runs them under the same resolved shell. No assertion was loosened to the observed output: each now asserts what a shell reads, and the mutation runs show it red when the path is not one word. Runs (all exit 0, '1/1 files ok, 407 cases'): `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_audit_status.py`, the same with `--spaced`, and with `--encoding cp1252`. Also a direct run under TMPDIR='<scratch>/via/s p', via being a link to real: every kt case PASS. In that run sl1-sl3 FAIL (404/407) only because the direct run keeps the session's CLAUDE_* variables, which `_cli` drops and `_in_project` does not. They pass under the sweep, and I did not touch them. ruff check on both files: exit 0. vermin -t=3.8-: exit 0. _output_lints.prose_number_claims() and house_style_violations(): 0 findings. NOT VERIFIED: Windows. I could not run the Windows legs. kt6b and kt8 now really run git worktree remove --force, update-ref and a submodule-foreach push to a C:\ path under git's sh there; until now they never ran on Windows (ran=None, saves=[]). The owner can check with `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_audit_status.py` on Windows; expected '1/1 files ok, 407 cases'. Dependants: audit-status.py renders byte-identical output, so /audit:status, /audit:worktree, drive-phase.py's kept-tree advice (P142.47/.49 aside keys, --force only for an aside key; kt9c still pins ASIDE_KEY), tests/test_drive_phase.py, tests/test_run_test_gate.py, tools/verify.sh, CONTRIBUTING.md, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, docs/examples/azure-pipelines.yml, docs/research/pipeline-cost-results.md and docs/demo-large.html stay correct: no behaviour or name changed. The test file's dependants stay correct as well. .github/sweep-costs.json: same cases, same spawn count; kt6b/kt8 now run through the resolved shell instead of a direct git/sh spawn, so the per-file cost is materially unchanged. tools/affected.py maps by path, unchanged. _live_copy.py and tests/test__status_facts.py are basename mentions; _cases, _fixture and _selftest are untouched.
outcome.descriptive: The kept-tree cases now judge a printed remover by the words a POSIX shell reads and run it as written, so they hold under a spaced or symlinked temp root and on Windows; the product's POSIX quoting was already right, and its target shell is now stated in the code.
